name: Inflammatory and Autoimmune Disease with Epilepsy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Autoimmune Epilepsy

criteria.description: Presence of recurrent unprovoked seizures consistent with epilepsy
Detection of specific autoantibodies associated with neuronal antigens (e.g., anti-NMDA receptor, anti-LGI1)
Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis showing pleocytosis or elevated protein indicating CNS inflammation
MRI evidence of inflammatory changes in limbic or other brain regions
Clinical improvement of seizures and neurological symptoms following immunotherapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent seizures plus detection of neuronal autoantibodies; supportive findings such as inflammatory CSF or MRI changes strengthen diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of epilepsy and confirmation of autoimmune etiology.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Refractory focal seizures with impaired awareness
pathognomonic.notes: Seizures often resistant to conventional antiepileptic drugs
Characterized by memory impairment and behavioral changes
searchTerms: inflammation causing memory and mood changes

common.notes: Often progressive over weeks to months

common.symptomName: Psychiatric manifestations such as anxiety or psychosis
Fever or constitutional symptoms during active inflammation

occasional.symptomName: Autonomic dysfunction including tachycardia or blood pressure instability
searchTerms: fast heart rate or unstable blood pressure

occasional.notes: Often associated with active CNS inflammation

occasional.symptomName: Sleep disturbances including insomnia or hypersomnia
searchTerms: too much or too little sleep

occasional.symptomName: Peripheral neuropathy symptoms such as paresthesia
searchTerms: peripheral nerve symptoms like pins and needles
skin inflammation with blood vessel damage
red or purple skin spots from vessel inflammation

rare.notes: Rare but possible systemic autoimmune manifestation
searchTerms: kidney problems with protein in urine

laboratory: Presence of neuronal autoantibodies (e.g., anti-NMDA receptor, anti-LGI1, anti-CASPR2)
imaging: MRI showing hyperintensities in medial temporal lobes or limbic structures
FDG-PET demonstrating hypermetabolism in affected brain regions
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible HLA associations in some cases
other: Positive response to immunotherapy (e.g., corticosteroids, IVIG, plasmapheresis)

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of viral DNA/RNA in CSF
Rapid onset with fever and systemic infection signs
Absence of inflammatory markers or autoantibodies
Paraneoplastic antibodies distinct from autoimmune epilepsy markers

redFlags: Failure to respond to standard antiepileptic drugs
references: Lancaster E. The diagnosis and treatment of autoimmune encephalitis. J Clin Neurol. 2016.
Graus F, et al. A clinical approach to diagnosis of autoimmune encephalitis. Lancet Neurol. 2016.
Dubey D, et al. Autoimmune epilepsy: clinical characteristics and response to immunotherapy. Epilepsia. 2017.
